name: Why is a truly curbless shower sometimes not possible in an older San Diego home?

mainEntity.name: Why is a truly curbless shower sometimes not possible in an older San Diego home?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A curbless shower is not automatically the best option for a home with an older slab, limited floor depth, or a tight existing layout. The floor may need careful planning to create drainage slope without creating an abrupt transition elsewhere. Elite Remodeling & Design can evaluate the existing conditions during bathroom design.

A low-profile threshold may offer better water containment and a more predictable construction path when a fully level entry is impractical.

Key factors:
- Slab or framing depth
- Drain location and required slope
- Adjacent finished-floor height
- Waterproofing continuity at the entry

Ask for the proposed finished-floor elevations, not only a visual rendering. Compare curbless and low-threshold options based on access, water control, and construction complexity.

The safest-looking concept must also work with the building’s existing structure.
acceptedAnswer.description: Limited floor depth, slab conditions, drain location, and the surrounding finished-floor height can make a fully level entry difficult. A low threshold may provide better water control with fewer structural compromises. Request finished elevations and compare both options before deciding.
